summary: Hayes Valley is where the city kept its horses. In one decade the Board licensed 125 of them at 416-418 Fulton Street, ninety-four behind 1820 Market Street, sixty-eight at 1215 Fell Street, fifty at 525 Gough — and five ponies at 915 Fulton. Then the same addresses came back as garages: 1213-1215 Fell Street was the Divisadero Street Stables in 1914 and a public garage the year after. Before any of that, in the spring of 1906, the Board's attention was called to Camp Forrest, a relief station on Laguna Street between Hayes and Fell, and to the way rations were being handed out there. The far end of Hayes Street was too steep for a plain roadway and got retaining walls, steps and railings in 1915, with a lamp at each stairway. City Hall was ordered built at the neighbourhood's eastern edge in 1913 and the High School of Commerce enlarged on Fell Street in 1922, and through those same years the Board moved Fell, Gough and Page Streets out of the residential zone and into the commercial one, block by block, while licensing the fuel-oil tank under each building — a dairy at 231 Franklin Street, a laundry on Fulton. From 2001 the record turns almost entirely to Octavia Boulevard: parking rules written to take effect once it was "completed and open for traffic", a new green handed to the Recreation and Park Department in 2005, supportive housing built on a leftover Central Freeway parcel on Fulton Street in 2008, and a plan drawn for the square mile around its junction with Market Street. Between those, steadily since the 1990s, the flats have been cut into condominiums and each new bar and shop on Hayes Street has come to the Board for its licence.
